content:
kevin: ran the apples-to-apples pass with strict parameter sync across runtimes. attached numbers below.

kevin: test setup: same prompts, stop sequences, tokenizer vocab mapping, decoding params (temp=0.0, top_p=1.0, beam=1), seed=42. used replay harness for live traffic vs synthetic generator.

kevin: command we used:
```
./harness/replay --source=perf/replays/2025-02-12.prod.json \n  --runtime=redwood_local:port --concurrency=64 --rate=200rps \n  --seed=42 --decode-config='{"temperature":0.0,"top_p":1.0,"stop":["\n\n"],"max_tokens":256}'
```

maria: nice. did you pin kernel selection? we need identical kernels (fp16 vs int8) across runs, otherwise apples fail.

kevin: yes pinned: KERNEL_POLICY=force_fp16 on runtime-A, force_int8 for runtime-B. but we also ran a force-kernel-override test to ensure same math path.

ara: how did you handle KV cache? replay harness had mixed session lengths. cold vs warm cache makes big diff.

kevin: split metrics by cache state. we replayed each user session twice: first pass cold (new session id), second pass warm (replay immediate). p95 gets ~12% better on warm cache.

gina: can you paste the perf summary? p50/p95/p99 and tokens/sec plus token-per-cost delta?

kevin: summary table (excerpt):
```
runtime-A (fp16): p50=45ms p95=120ms p99=240ms tokens/s=380 cost_per_k=0.12
runtime-B (int8): p50=48ms p95=140ms p99=300ms tokens/s=410 cost_per_k=0.08
apples diff (exact param-match): latency_regression_on_int8_p99=+25% when stop-seq misaligned
```

maria: stop-seq misaligned? we thought tokenizer alignment took care of that.

kevin: that's where apples diverged. one runtime used tokenizer.encode with add_special_tokens=true, other false. resulted in different stop offsets, so some responses ran longer.

ara: oof. we should canonicalize tokenizer pipeline: explicit encode call + decode normalizer. add a unit test that ensures length equality for canonical prompts.

gina: also verify decoding hooks: streaming chunk boundaries can change early-stop behavior if the stop detector is applied per-chunk vs full output.

ci-bot: perf-checker: regression alert on branch release/rt-1.4: p99 increased by 18% for int8 compared to base. (scan-id: perf-178201)

kevin: that CI alert corresponds to the kernel selection change we made last week. I ran a kernel profiler: found a hot path in rotary mul implementation that becomes heavier on int8 path for short sequences.

maria: can you paste profiler snippet?

kevin: profiler excerpt:
```
hotspot: rotary_mul_forward (int8_pack) 42%
   next: attention_kv_write 18%
   next: kv_cache_lookup 9%
```

ara: actionable: 1) force identical tokenizer settings 2) replay harness should mark session cache state explicit 3) add deterministic stop-seq tests in apples harness 4) kernel micro-optim for rotary on int8.

gina: I'll own tests (3). will add a tiny harness that fuzzes stop sequences across chunk boundaries and asserts same truncation point.

kevin: for load testing methodology notes:
- always run both synthetic generator and replay on same commit; synthetic to stress throughput, replay for fidelity.
- seed RNG + deterministic sampling for greedy/temp=0 tests.
- separate cold/warm KV cache buckets in metrics.
- pin tokenizer flags and include a binary hash of tokenizer config in run metadata.

maria: also include kernel selection policy in the result metadata: kernel_name + kernel_hash. then apples runner can compare and fail if mismatched (or automatically remap token offsets).

ara: can we have loadbot annotate runs with cache-warm tags? loadbot: any plans?

loadbot: added tag support. use --tags cache:warm or cache:cold, will appear in run metadata.

kevin: final ask: for the regression PR I'll attach the harness artifacts and a minimal reproducer with 3 sessions (short/long/mid). want review from eng-runtime + eng-ml.

gina: ack, will review tests.

maria: I'll pair with kevin on the rotary int8 micro-opt.

kevin: thanks :thumbsup:
